questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Memory versus computation trade-offs” in this lesson?
options: This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Check device/dtype placement and measure memory or numerical behavior on the actual target hardware; optional acceleration is not guaranteed.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
questions.answer_key: Check device/dtype placement and measure memory or numerical behavior on the actual target hardware; optional acceleration is not guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Memory versus computation trade-offs: Check device/dtype placement and measure memory or numerical behavior on the actual target hardware; optional acceleration is not guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Recomputation during backward propagation”, what should a learner verify?
options: confirm model and input devices match, supported dtype/device combinations are used, and the measured result is numerically acceptable.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
questions.answer_key: confirm model and input devices match, supported dtype/device combinations are used, and the measured result is numerically acceptable.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: confirm model and input devices match, supported dtype/device combinations are used, and the measured result is numerically acceptable.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Choosing checkpointed regions”?
options: Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
questions.answer_key: Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not treat a GPU availability check as proof that all model operators or precision modes are supported.
